transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-27
Start time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Morgan (Redwood AE), Alex (Redwood SE), Renee (Redwood CSM), Sarah (Hearthline Legal), Jamal (Procurement), Priya (CTO), Benji (Platform)

Summary:
Quick intake to align MSA/DPA redline ownership, onboarding playbook sequencing (legal -> procurement -> platform), and a short technical sanity check comparing hosted vs dedicated for their latency-sensitive features. High level agreement to proceed with redlines and a short benchmark run.

Topics:
- MSA redlines and DPA-specific retention/KMS clauses
- SLA thresholds and remedies (Uptime, P99, escalation path)
- Network and data residency (VPC peering, egress limits, air-gap concerns)
- Pricing approval path and pilot/PO thresholds
- Onboarding playbook and timelines

Transcript:
00:00 Morgan: Okay thanks everyone for joining, I think we have about 50 minutes blocked, we wanted to go over the MSA/DPA orchestration stuff and also carve out a short tech check, is that still what people wanted?
00:07 Sarah: Yes, that sounds good. We just need to make sure legal and procurement are aligned before we go into the pilots.
00:12 Jamal: Yeah and the vendor committee sits early December so we need things pretty buttoned up.
00:16 Morgan: Right, and logistically we found it easiest to run MSA redlines first and then DPA follow-up, but open to your workflow. Alex will also do a quick perf check so you have the numbers for procurement.
00:27 Alex: Hi all, quick background — Redwood supports hosted, dedicated, and private deployments, and depending on your token throughput and latency SLOs the cost/latency tradeoff changes. I'll scope a small benchmark with a subset of your traffic profile.
00:39 Priya: For our use case the P99 under 150ms is important on search rerank calls. We can tolerate higher tail on background embedding jobs but the user-facing ones are sensitive.
00:48 Alex: Got it. We'll test with 32-token prompts and the 512 token KV cache path, roughly mirror your production pattern.
00:56 Benji: Quick question — are you asking for VPC peering or full on-prem appliance? We're leaning toward VPC private deployment with customer-managed keys.
01:03 Morgan: Both are options. For regulated data we usually recommend Private (VPC) with KMS integration — Redwood Private gives you a private control plane and KMS/HSM hooks. If you need air-gap we have an on-prem package but procurement usually wants to avoid that unless absolutely needed.
01:15 Sarah: On the DPA, primary ask from legal is limiting retention to 90 days for model logs and 180 days for audit logs, and of course standard deletion on request. Also need SOC2 attestation and subprocessor list.
01:25 Renee: We can share the SOC2 report and subprocessor registry. For logs we also have configurable retention at route level, we can map that to your retention policy.
01:34 Sarah: Perfect. Also need a clause that says KMS keys are customer-managed and that Redwood cannot decrypt with master key — is that the standard wording?
01:42 Morgan: We can add a KMS-holder clause, we usually accept customer-managed keys via our KMS integration, the MSA/DPA language usually states that the customer controls the key and Redwood only processes ciphertext. I'll put proposed language in the redlines.
01:51 Jamal: On pricing, procurement wants to see an anchor for pilot spend and then commit thresholds. We normally approve a pilot up to $25k without executive sign off. Above that we need committee.
02:00 Morgan: OK we can structure a pilot agreement: $20k credit for a 6-week pilot, then a dedicated capacity estimate if you choose to reserve. Alex can show cost deltas.
02:08 Priya: The tricky bit is the caching behavior — for user session affinity we need deterministic KV caching so embedding latencies stay low. If caching affects caching hit rates across tenants, that could be an issue.
02:19 Alex: Right, we do prefix and KV caching tied to tenant routes; if you want isolation we can put you on dedicated pools so cache isn't shared. That has a cost impact but predictable latency. I'll include cache hit rate assumptions in the doc.
02:31 Benji: On networking, we need details on egress IPs and can we use static egress? Our firewall team needs explicit IP allowlist.
02:39 Morgan: Yes, for Dedicated/Private you get static egress pools or can use VPC peering. For hosted we hand out ranges but they're larger; procurement usually wants peering for tighter control.
02:48 Sarah: A legal question — indemnity and data breach notification windows, we prefer 72 hours. Is that okay?
02:53 Morgan: 72 hours is within our standard escalation in enterprise plans, we'll capture that in the MSA.
02:58 Jamal: Also want to confirm subprocessor carveouts — if you onboard a new subprocessors who has access to PII, we need a 30-day notification window.
03:06 Renee: We can add a notification clause and a subprocessor update cadence. Our subprocessor registry link will be in the shared folder.
03:12 Priya: From an engineering view, the onboarding playbook — what are the steps, who performs them, and how long each takes? We need an explicit runbook for platform handoff.
03:21 Morgan: Good point. Typical playbook: legal sign-off -> procurement approval -> technical kickoff (networking, KMS, test keys) -> smoke perf run -> pilot -> production rollout. Usually the technical kickoff is 1 week, pilot 4–6 weeks, rollout depends on results. We'll layout a timeline.
03:33 Benji: For the test keys, can you give us both a staging and production KMS workflow? We want to test key rotation too.
03:40 Alex: Yep, we'll provide a staging KMS flow and a rotation test plan; we'll document the steps to rotate without downtime using our key-rotation helpers.
03:48 Sarah: For the DPA, also want language around deletion attestations — i.e., Redwood will provide a deletion certificate when requested. Is that feasible?
03:55 Morgan: We can provide confirmation of deletion and a log of when deletion operations happened, that's part of our audit logs.
03:59 Jamal: Procurement will also run a mini security questionnaire — do you have a standard one we can use?
04:05 Renee: We have a vendor security questionnaire template and our security team can fill the parts for you; we'll also attach the SOC2 and penetration test summary.
04:12 Priya: Back to pricing — if we go dedicated, what's the expected monthly minimum for a pool that hits our latency targets?
04:19 Alex: Ballpark — depends on GPU class and reserved slots; for your P99 target on rerank we'd likely recommend a 2x-GPU dedicated pool, normally that maps to a baseline commit in the mid-five figures monthly. I'll produce an estimate with options (spot/dedicated/burst).
04:32 Jamal: To get procurement to sign off faster, we need a one-page summary that maps compliance controls to clauses and shows pilot spend and timelines. Can you provide that?
04:39 Morgan: Yes — action: Morgan will create a one-pager compliance map + pilot terms.
04:44 Sarah: On export controls — do you ship models or weights? We need to confirm no models with restricted export are involved.
04:50 Morgan: We only serve inference requests; model artifacts are not exported to customers except through agreed workflows. We'll include a clause clarifying that.
04:58 Priya: Are there any competitors' terms we should be aware of that might cause procurement to push back?
05:02 Jamal: They asked about Anthropic's policy and Azure's pricing credit — if another vendor offers lower pilot cost that might sway the committee.
05:09 Morgan: Understood, we'll make the case on predictability and unit economics; Alex's perf/cost doc should help.
05:14 Alex: I'll also include tail latency graphs and a simple cost per 1k tokens comparison across profiles.
05:20 Benji: Can you include a sample SLA with a P99 target and the remedy schedule? Procurement often wants explicit credits.
05:26 Morgan: We'll draft a sample SLA: 99.9% uptime with service credits tiers at 99.5/99.0 thresholds and escalation contact list. Legal may want different language but it's a starting point.
05:36 Sarah: We may ask to limit liability in the MSA — usual — is that open for negotiation?
05:41 Morgan: Yes that's standard negotiation territory, we'll flag the uncommon asks early.
05:45 Jamal: Final question — does Redwood support SSO via SAML/OAuth and RBAC? We need admin provisioning mapped to our identity provider.
05:52 Renee: Yes we support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning for users, and role-based access controls. We'll share the integration guide.
05:58 Priya: Great. If you can get redlines to us within a week we can prep the vendor committee packet.
06:02 Morgan: We'll aim to have draft redlines and the one-pager by next Thursday.
06:06 (crosstalk)
06:09 Morgan: Ok let's recap next steps quickly...
06:12 Morgan: Recap — Morgan will upload MSA/DPA redlines, the one-page compliance/pilot summary, and the proposed SLA sample. Alex will run a small benchmark and cost delta doc. Renee will push SOC2 and security questionnaire. Sarah and Jamal will confirm committee date and provide regulatory retention specs. Benji will share network diagram.
06:30 Sarah: That sounds right. Thanks everyone.
06:33 Morgan: Thanks all — we'll follow up in the shared folder with links.
